name: Nellukkadai Mariamman Temple
significance: A Mariamman shrine in Nagapattinam town with a rajagopura and prakara, run by the Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department. Besides the four-armed goddess it houses shrines to Vinayaka, Subramanya, Kathavaraya Swamy, Periyachchi, Ayyanar and Ellaiyamman.

name: Achankovil Sastha Temple
deity: Shasta (Achankovil Arasan), with consorts Purna and Pushkala
significance: A forest shrine on the Achankovil river where Shasta is worshipped in his householder form flanked by Purna and Pushkala, unlike the celibate Ayyappan of Sabarimala. It is best known as a healing shrine for snakebite: sandalwood paste and holy water from the idol's right palm are given as medicine, and the sanctum is opened at night for victims.
story: The image is said to have been consecrated by Parashurama.

name: Sree Krishna Swami Temple, Thodupuzha
significance: The principal Krishna temple of Thodupuzha town, standing on the bank of the Thodupuzhayar. The article records that a raja of Keezhmalanadu built the shrine and consecrated the image; tantric rights belong to the Aramallur Kavanattu Mana.
story: A Brahmin pilgrim resting here is said to have received a vision of Krishna, bathed in the river and worshipped him on the Chothi day of Meenam, the day still kept as the temple's origin.

name: Santhoor Subramanya Temple
significance: A coastal Karnataka shrine where Kartikeya is worshipped as Subramanya, lord of serpents. Its main draw is the Shashti Mahotsav, alongside Kiru Shashti and Nagara Panchami, which brings thousands of pilgrims to the village.

name: Siddheshwar Temple, Solapur
significance: Solapur's central temple, set within a lake, built by the yogi Siddharameshwar, a 12th-century Shiva devotee revered as a god in the Lingayat faith, who took samadhi here in 1167 CE and installed sixty-eight lingams in the courtyard. A marble samadhi marks the spot, and the temple and lake have been managed by the Shri Siddheshwar Devsthan Panch Committee since 1899.
story: Solapur is said to have begun prospering from the moment Siddheshwar was born.

name: Nava Toran Temple
significance: An 11th-century Varaha temple at Khor named for the decorative arches, ten of them set in two rows, that frame it. Its carving includes leaf-shaped borders and makara heads.
story: A tunnel is said to run from beneath the temple to Chittor Fort, used by Maharana Pratap to come and worship here.

name: Karat Shiva Temple
builtDisplay: c. 1,000 years old; rebuilt after 18th-c. destruction
significance: A hill-country Shiva temple near Mananthavady reckoned about a thousand years old, destroyed in the 18th century during Tipu Sultan's campaigns. It was rebuilt through an effort led by Krishnan Nambeesan with help from residents of several faiths, and the reconsecration is marked each year on 10-11 May.

name: Narapura Venkateswara Temple, Jammalamadugu
significance: An old Venkateswara shrine at Jammalamadugu in the Rayalaseema country, whose administration was handed to the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams on 23 October 2008.
story: The temple takes its name from Narapuraiah, a devotee said to have built it in the form he believed the god wished.

name: Shri Raghunath Ji Temple
significance: A roughly 650-year-old Rama and Sita temple beside the Jalsen reservoir at Hindaun City, credited in the article to Tulsidas. Diwali, Rama Navami and Dussehra are its principal festivals.

name: Abhaya Varadeeswarar Temple
deity: Shiva as Abhaya Varadeeswarar, with Parvati as Kadal Partha Nayaki
significance: A coastal Shiva temple in Adirampattinam whose original complex is attributed to the Cholas, with the standing masonry structure raised by later ruling powers. It is maintained by the Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department.
story: Devas beaten in war by the asuras are said to have worshipped Shiva here on the thirteenth lunar day under the star Adhira, and because he sheltered them he is called Abhaya Varadha, the giver of refuge.

name: Kiruthivakesvarar Temple, Sulamangalam
deity: Shiva as Kiruthivakesvarar (lingam), with the goddess Alankaravalli
significance: A Shiva temple on the Thanjavur-Kumbakonam road whose lingam is called Kiruthivakesvarar and whose goddess is Alankaravalli. It is counted among the shrines associated with the Nayanar saint Appar.
story: Shiva is said to have taken this name after killing the asura Kayasuran who was tormenting the people, and Parvati is held to have performed penance at the site.

name: Brahmapureeswarar Temple, Thiruppattur
deity: Shiva as Brahmapureeswarar (swayambhu lingam), with Brahma Sampath Gowri
significance: A Shiva temple at Thiruppattur in Tiruchirappalli district, unusual for its association with Brahma, who is said to have installed twelve lingams here. It is administered by the Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department.
story: Brahma, punished by Shiva with the loss of his fifth head for his pride, is said to have come here in penance, worshipped beneath a magizha tree, and had his curse lifted and his powers of creation restored.

name: Roda Group of Temples
deity: Shiva, Vishnu, Surya, Ganesha and the Navagraha across seven shrines
style: Maha-Gurjara (Anarta school), latina and phansana spires
significance: A group of seven small stone shrines about 18 km from Himmatnagar, raised over perhaps two centuries during the tripartite struggle between the Gurjara-Pratiharas and Rashtrakutas. Scholars treat them as the ancestor of the later Solanki or Maru-Gurjara manner, and an idol inscription at the site is dated Samvat 1104 (1048 CE).

name: Thiru Nayathode Siva Narayana Temple
significance: A twin-deity temple near Cochin International Airport where Shiva and Mahavishnu are worshipped together, its founding attributed to Cheraman Perumal Nayanar. It is a protected monument under the Kerala Department of Archaeology.

name: Ratneshwar Mahadev Temple
significance: Varanasi's celebrated leaning temple, standing at the foot of Manikarnika Ghat with a tilt of about nine degrees and its sanctum flooded for much of the year. Revenue records date it to 1825-30, though its patron is disputed between a servant of Raja Man Singh, the Amethi royal house, Baija Bai of Gwalior and Ratna Bai, a servant of Ahilya Bai of Indore.
story: One account holds that Ahilya Bai cursed the temple to lean because her servant Ratna Bai had named it after herself.

name: Shri Viswa Vinayaka Mandir, Rhenock
significance: A four-storeyed Ganesha temple 108 feet tall on a 2.56-acre site in eastern Sikkim, housing fifty-one forms of the god. Its foundation was laid on 20 April 2008 and it was inaugurated on 3 October 2016, built with materials from Thailand and craftsmen from Nepal and West Bengal.

name: Shree Brahma Baidarkala Garadi Kshetra
significance: A garadi shrine on the Mangalore-Bangalore highway about 4 km from central Mangalore, sacred to the Tuluva community. It venerates the twin heroes Koti and Chennayya, placed by the article in the period c. 1556-1591 CE.

name: Aryadurga Devi Temple, Devihasol
significance: A goddess temple in Devihasol village of Rajapur taluka, about 18 km from Rajapur and 380 km from Mumbai, and a regional centre of Devi worship in the Konkan. The article gives no coordinates, so the Wikidata point is used.
story: The shrine is said to stand where the goddess appeared for a moment before an aged devotee named Palsule Desai and vanished, leaving her footprints inside the mandir; she is also remembered for destroying the demon Vratsaru.

name: Sundernath Temple
significance: A major historic Shiva temple of the Mithila region, standing close to the India-Nepal border in Araria district. It draws worshippers from northern Bihar and southern Nepal, especially at Maha Shivaratri and on Purnima days.

name: Uttara Guruvayurappan Temple
significance: Delhi's Guruvayurappan temple, founded on 17 May 1983 by the Arsha Dharma Parishad and completed on the same date in 1989, modelled on the Kerala shrine of the same deity. Built in Kerala style with gopurams to east and west and a two-chambered sanctum, it is a focus of the city's Malayali and Tamil communities.

name: Tulja Bhavani Temple, Peddamunigal
significance: A Tulja Bhavani temple built in the mid-1950s by Kethavath Chandru Naik with local support, standing above the Krishna river near Nagarjuna Sagar Dam on the edge of the Nallamala forest.
story: The goddess is said to have come to the aid of Anubuti, a sage's wife whose penance on the Mandakini was being disturbed by the demon Kukur, and to have taken the name Tulja Bhavani after destroying him.
